amstar2_items.justification: Explicitly used the PICOC framework (Section 2.1, pp. 5-6) defining Population (slum dwellers), Intervention/Exposure (access to housing and WASH services), Outcomes (experiences around access inequalities), and Context (urban/peri-urban slums in LMICs in Latin America, Sub-Saharan Africa, and South Asia).

Authors state that a JBI scoping review protocol exists in online Appendix 1, but explicitly report it was not pre-registered ('was not registered to accommodate the potential evolution of the topic', p. 5) and no risk-of-bias assessment plan was included.

Explicitly justified including qualitative and mixed-methods designs and excluding strictly quantitative studies (p. 7) to capture power dynamics and lived experiences and avoid national survey averages masking vulnerable slum populations.

Searched three databases (PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science) in November 2022 with synonym lists and search strings in Appendices 2-3 and stated reasons for English-only and peer-reviewed-only limits (pp. 5-7), meeting Partial Yes, but explicitly excluded grey literature and did not report reference-list checking, registry searches, or expert consultation.

Two reviewers independently screened the 102 deduplicated titles/abstracts in Rayyan, but full-text eligibility screening of the 57 remaining articles was performed by only one reviewer without duplicate verification or kappa agreement testing (p. 7).
Data extraction for the 33 included studies was performed by a single author in Excel without duplicate extraction or independent verification reported (p. 7).

24 articles were excluded at full-text screening (p. 7), but no list of excluded full-text studies with study-specific exclusion reasons is provided in the article or cited appendices (and Figure 1 renders as blank whitespace on PDF p. 8).

Narrative text describes settings, populations, and substantive barriers, and online Appendix 4 extracts author, year, geographical focus, focus domain, study population, barriers, consequences, and recommendations (p. 7), though detailed study designs, sample sizes, and study timeframes are not reported inline.
Consistent with standard JBI scoping review conventions, no risk-of-bias or methodological quality appraisal of the 33 included qualitative and mixed-methods primary studies was conducted.
Sources of funding for the 33 included primary studies were not extracted or reported.
No meta-analysis was conducted; strictly quantitative studies were excluded by design and synthesis was qualitative/thematic.
Because no critical appraisal or risk-of-bias assessment of included studies was performed, study quality/risk of bias was not accounted for when interpreting and discussing review findings.
Authors substantively discuss contextual, regional, settlement-level, socio-economic, and intersectional social-identity heterogeneity across the included studies in both Results and Discussion.
No quantitative synthesis or meta-analysis was conducted.
Explicitly reports no potential conflict of interest and discloses funding from Utrecht University via the UU Mosaic fund PhD grant (PDF p. 18).

methodological_notes: 1. Review Design & Scope: Self-described JBI scoping review (Peters et al., 2020) synthesizing qualitative and mixed-methods peer-reviewed journal articles (2000-2022, English) on access inequalities to WASH and housing in urban/peri-urban slums in Latin America, Sub-Saharan Africa, and South Asia. Strictly quantitative studies and grey literature were excluded by design. Narrow Criterion 2 is rated borderline_narrow_c2 because legal/tenure/regulatory mechanisms (settlement legal status, land tenure security, landlord-tenant agreements, housing formalisation, eviction risk, and pay-per-use toilet pricing) are substantively synthesized in Sections 3.2, 3.3.3, and 3.3.4, but constitute one strand within a broader lived-experience scoping review where many included studies examine MHM stigma, gender roles, or physical latrine conditions rather than legal/institutional rules. 2. AMSTAR 2 Fit & Quality: AMSTAR 2 is a borderline fit for a JBI scoping review that neither aims to pool effect sizes nor conducts risk-of-bias appraisal. Under AMSTAR 2, confidence is Critically Low due to multiple critical flaws: unregistered protocol without RoB plan (Q2), no list of the 24 excluded full-text articles (Q7; note also Figure 1 PRISMA graphic renders blank on PDF p. 8), no RoB appraisal (Q9), and no consideration of RoB in synthesis (Q13), alongside single-reviewer full-text screening (Q5) and single-author data extraction (Q6). 3. Primary-Study Extraction & Bibliographic Audit: Appendices 1-4 (including the formal Appendix 4 data extraction table) are external online supplements not printed in the PDF, so included_studies_list_completeness is partial_inline_citations_only. However, auditing all empirical citations across Results Section 3 (excluding the external conceptual comparison Rigon, 2022 in 3.1 and the UN-Habitat grey-literature discussion paper Singh, S. D. et al., 2022 in 3.4.1) yields exactly 33 unique peer-reviewed journal articles (2000-2022), matching the reported N = 33 count 1-for-1. Note two reference-manager metadata corruptions in the published Reference list (PDF p. 20): both Kwiringira et al. (2014, BMC Public Health 14) and Munn et al. (2018, BMC Med Res Methodol 18) had their titles and DOIs overwritten with Article #1 of their respective BMC volumes.
